environment.name: PIKIT_ADMIN_TOKEN
environment.description: Bearer token of the operators (the dashboard); at least 32 characters (for example `openssl rand -hex 32`).

environment.name: TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN
environment.description: The bot's token from @BotFather; `pikit configure` asks for it and checks it.

environment.name: TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS
environment.description: Telegram user ids allowed to talk to the bot, separated by commas; `pikit configure` fills it when you message the bot. Deployed without the CLI, it may stay empty: the owner logs in with TELEGRAM_PASSWORD instead.

environment.name: TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET
environment.description: What Telegram sends with every update, so only Telegram reaches your agent; `pikit configure` generates it, and `pikit up` gives it to Telegram.

environment.name: TELEGRAM_PASSWORD
environment.description: Optional password of 8 characters or more: send `/login <password>` to the bot, and that chat may talk to it from then on. Whoever knows it can log in; change it to log everyone out. The Deploy to Cloudflare button's way to let its owner in.

environment.name: OPENROUTER_API_KEY
environment.description: An OpenRouter API key (openrouter.ai/settings/keys). Read by pi-ai only when model.credentials stores nothing for openrouter.

environment.name: BRAVE_API_KEY
environment.description: A Brave Search API key, from api-dashboard.search.brave.com (the free plan works). Optional: without it the app starts and each search fails saying so. Read through secrets; the model never sees it.
